sectionTitle: Concrete work in St. Thomas and Elgin County
intro: St. Thomas grew up as a railway town, and that history shows up in its housing stock — brick homes on narrow in-town lots alongside newer development toward the Southgate area. Both need different approaches to driveway and patio work.

blocks.text: Railway-era brick homes and their narrow driveways

Neighbourhoods close to the historic downtown and the old rail yards have some of the oldest housing stock in Elgin County — many brick homes built in the late 1800s and early 1900s with narrow single-track driveways, if a driveway exists at all. When we work on these properties, the constraints are usually about width and access rather than soil: mature trees, tight side yards, and sometimes a driveway that needs to run alongside a foundation with limited clearance for equipment. We plan excavation carefully around these older foundations, which in some cases sit on shallower footings than current building code would allow.

A common request from owners of these older St. Thomas homes is widening a single-car driveway into a two-car surface, which sometimes means working close to a shared property line with a neighbour. We handle the layout and, where needed, the setback confirmation as part of the quote so the finished driveway sits correctly on the property.
Lynhurst, Southgate and Mitchell Hepburn: newer subdivisions

Lynhurst and the Southgate area represent St. Thomas's more recent growth, with wider lots, attached double garages, and driveways poured to current subdivision standards. These are usually straightforward new-driveway or replacement jobs, and most of the questions we get here are about finish upgrades — stamped concrete, exposed aggregate, or integral colour to complement newer brick and siding combinations. The Mitchell Hepburn area, closer to the Elgin County fairgrounds, has a similar mix of newer builds where we frequently pour matching driveway and walkway combinations in a single visit.
Working near the Port Stanley road corridor

A number of St. Thomas properties sit along or near the Port Stanley Road corridor, on lots that transition from urban to more rural character as you head south toward the lake. These properties sometimes have longer driveways with more grade change than a typical in-town lot, which changes how we plan slope and drainage across the pour.

St. Thomas and the surrounding Elgin County area sit on clay loam soils similar to London's, though drainage can vary noticeably from block to block depending on how the original subdivision was graded. On older streets near downtown, we sometimes find drainage patterns that were never properly corrected when the original driveway was poured decades ago — water pooling at the garage apron or running toward the house foundation instead of away from it. Replacing the driveway is our chance to correct that grading permanently, not just repeat the old mistake in new concrete.
St. Thomas is one of our most active service areas outside London — see current driveway pricing and finish options at /concrete-driveways-st-thomas.
Matching concrete colour on an existing St. Thomas property

Because so many St. Thomas homes have concrete walkways, porches or patios installed at different times, colour matching comes up often — a homeowner wants a new driveway or patio section that doesn't look mismatched against existing concrete. We bring integral colour and colour hardener samples to the on-site estimate so you can compare against your existing concrete in daylight before committing to a colour.
Retaining walls and patios for St. Thomas's sloped lots

Several St. Thomas neighbourhoods, particularly those closer to Kettle Creek and the ravines that cut through town, have noticeable elevation changes between the street and the backyard. A poured concrete retaining wall is a practical way to reclaim usable yard space on these lots, and we frequently pair a retaining wall project with a new patio slab so the levelled area is immediately usable rather than left as bare fill.

faqs.q: Can you widen a narrow driveway on an older St. Thomas brick home?
faqs.a: Yes, this is one of our most common requests in the older parts of St. Thomas. We assess property line setbacks and any nearby foundation clearance during the free estimate before quoting the widening.

faqs.q: Do you work around shallow foundations on century homes in St. Thomas?
faqs.a: We do. Older brick homes near the downtown core sometimes have shallower footings than current code requires, so we plan excavation depth and equipment placement carefully to avoid disturbing the foundation.

faqs.q: How do you fix a driveway that drains toward the house instead of away from it?
faqs.a: This is a grading problem from the original pour, and the only permanent fix is to remove the old slab and re-form it with correct slope. We assess drainage direction during every St. Thomas estimate and correct it as part of the replacement.

faqs.q: Do you serve properties along the Port Stanley Road corridor near St. Thomas?
faqs.a: Yes, properties along that corridor are within our regular St. Thomas and Elgin County service area, and we do not charge additional travel fees for them.
